summary: I sent the bounded brief, which never asks to be shown anything. The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, then read NOTES.md, the page files and all four UI guideline docs. An auto-compaction landed between the skill load and the first question ("Skills restored (hyperpowers:brainstorming)"). The agent still classed the task as bounded and kept the design in chat. For the layout question it started the visual companion on its own (start-server.sh), gave a localhost URL, and wrote filter-placement.html with three candidate layouts (A/B/C). I picked A. It then asked its non-visual questions in the terminal, posted a design summary in chat, asked for approval, and started work once I said yes. No spec or plan file was created.
reasoning: All 8 criteria pass, each backed by the session log, files on disk, or screen text. Even with an auto-compaction between the skill load and the first visual question, the agent worked out on its own that the layout question was better shown than described, without any visual cue from me. It opened the companion only at that question, kept the task bounded with no spec or plan, asked for approval before writing code, and started implementation after I approved.

observations.description: On first run Claude Code showed a 'Newer Opus model available — Update settings to use Opus 5.5?' prompt even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5 and the header later showed 'Opus 5.5'. Choosing No worked, but the prompt is confusing when the model is already pinned on the command line.
The trust-folder and bypass-permissions dialogs both have 'No, exit' selected by default. That is easy to hit by accident in an automated run.

The agent pointed out that the companion writes under .hyperpowers/ and the repo has no .gitignore entry for it, so .hyperpowers/ shows as untracked in git status. The skill could suggest the ignore entry or put companion files outside the repo.

Context use was very high. Auto-compaction ran once before the first question and again right after approval ('10% until auto-compact'), mostly because the agent read four long guideline docs plus the skill and companion docs, and re-read guideline docs after approval.
The agent's message said the companion tab 'uses a lot of tokens' and offered to switch to the terminal instead. That is honest, but it might discourage users from using the companion.

After my answer about failed sign-ins, security settings and one particular week, the agent widened the scope to include a date range, which was reasonable. It also asked an unprompted scope question about an existing no-JS blank-table issue. That was relevant but added a turn.
The agent asked me to explicitly approve adding a new public/tokens.css because the guidelines refer to a shared token sheet that doesn't exist in the repo. This is a good catch of a fixture gap.

criteria.evidence: Session log: the first tool_use is Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}. On screen: "Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill".

criteria.criterion: Visual companion opened with localhost URL and an HTML screen of candidate layouts
criteria.evidence: Log Bash: ".../skills/brainstorming/scripts/start-server.sh --project-dir \"$PWD\" --open". Screen: "http://localhost:54726/?key=7cc3ad0c...". File .hyperpowers/brainstorm/39465-1793828619/content/filter-placement.html (85 lines) has the headers "A: Inline filter bar above the table", "B: Quick-filter row above the table" and "C: Filter button with a popover panel".

criteria.criterion: Opened just-in-time; non-visual questions not routed through the browser
criteria.evidence: Before the companion started, the tool calls in the log were only reads (NOTES.md, page files, guideline docs, skill docs). It was started at the layout question: "The first decision is where the filter controls go on the page, and that's easier to show than describe." After my pick it wrote waiting.html ("Continuing in terminal..."). The questions about filter scope and no-JS were asked with terminal AskUserQuestion, not in the browser.
Screen: "I'm treating this as bounded. The filter only touches the existing activity page, so I'll give you a short design here in chat and skip the spec file." The design summary was posted in chat.
`ls docs` returned only `ui-guidelines`. `ls docs/superpowers docs/hyperpowers` returned "No such file or directory" for both. `git status --short` showed only `?? .hyperpowers/`.

criteria.criterion: No plan document / writing-plans not invoked
criteria.evidence: A jq search of the log for Skill tool_use inputs returned only {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}. git status shows no new plan files.

criteria.criterion: Asked for approval of layout before writing implementation code
criteria.evidence: The agent asked "Have a look and tell me what you think here" and recommended A, then asked "Does this look right? I'll start once you say yes." Before my approval, the only Write calls in the log were companion HTML files under .hyperpowers/.

After my "Yes, looks right... Go ahead." the agent began re-reading the guideline docs to implement and then auto-compacted. It had already committed to "I'll start once you say yes". I ended the session before any code was written.
